analysis:
Examined four changed files; no supported security regression found.

Gemma4RequestGeometry.swift (head 12-77): refactors the stage initializer into a private parameterized init. It adds a tensor-parallel init (23-36) that requires ranks to be 1 or plan.size, kinds.count == plan.layerCount, and per-layer kind agreement. Per-rank head counts use integer division. Bounds checks are kept: maximumTokens is within contextTokens, the dtype allowlist applies, and capacity uses checked byte sum/product.

Gemma4TensorParallelChoice.swift: read() (47-54) validates shape, a non-negative integral token and the vocabulary bound. logprobs() refuses when the gather's lead differs from the greedy maximum.

Gemma4TensorParallelLanes.swift:
- The executor init (88-90) checks shard/rank/group size and requires the vocabulary below 2^24, so tokens are exact in FP32.
- exchange (96-105) checks shape, dtype and finiteness.
- The sampled path (186-188) converts the peer-summed Float with Int(token) before the range check at 190. A non-finite or huge value from a faulty peer could trap rather than throw. The peer is another cluster rank under the same operator (ADV-001 can already crash its own process), so this is not reported as a finding.
- reserveLane (292-316) rejects media, checks the deadline and requires charge <= capacityLimitBytes plus the admitCapture memory reserve.
- serveBatch (323-361) holds the operation lock, binds a request fingerprint to loadAgreement and batchOrdinal, polls memory, and on failure sweeps the prefix cache and fails control.
- agreeRequest (365-375) compares all four 64-bit words of SHA-256(request fingerprint, loadAgreement) across ranks.
- Logprobs are published only by rank 0.
- generateLanes/OracleLaneHost are an oracle/tool path with a trivial agree closure; its callers are not visible.

Gemma4TensorParallelLoadAgreement.swift: fingerprints mode, plan, prompt policy, selection, lanes, KV, quantization, prefix on/off and data-plane fields under a schema string.

Open question for integration (T-041/SEC-035): batch lanes reuse and store prompt prefixes via prefix.open / prefix.scopes(request) / prefix.store (Lanes 121, 132-133). Those implementations are not supplied. Integration must confirm that scopes(request) derive from the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, so cross-account reuse stays impossible. It must also confirm that captures from failed or non-clean lanes are discarded (132 discards when !clean). The memory-yield and sweep semantics of the TP prefix cache are likewise unverified.
